security_problem: The repository's verification entry point mutated the tree it was verifying. harness/check.sh ran `make fmt` (`go fmt ./...`), which rewrote tracked files. cmd/visor-workflow records a workspace snapshot digest before each command and rejects a later mismatch, so a single unformatted tracked file made an otherwise green task unreachable at HARNESS_VERIFIED with target_snapshot_mismatch. CI had no formatting check either, so the drift merged green, and no local hook warned the author.
required_behavior: One check-only script, scripts/check-gofmt, is the single formatting authority: it lists unformatted Go files, names them, and exits non-zero without rewriting anything; it fails closed on a Go file that does not parse, on a missing gofmt and on an empty file list. Its file list is NUL-delimited and comes from git (`git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z -- '*.go'`), so spaces, newlines, non-ASCII names and names beginning with a dash are data rather than flags, and ignored trees such as .worktrees/ stay out of scope. It does not select a Go toolchain: gofmt comes from the caller's PATH. harness/check.sh calls it instead of `make fmt` and records the command in its manifest; scripts/pre-commit calls the same script so an author is warned before pushing; the CI Lint job runs it so a non-zero exit fails the job. CONTRIBUTING.md tells a contributor that unformatted Go fails the harness, the hook and CI, and that `make fmt` is the fix. harness/invariants.md records the rule as H51.
failure_behavior: A non-gofmt-clean tree fails the harness, the pre-commit hook, CI and the contract's target command with the offending filenames printed; nothing is reformatted automatically, so recorded evidence keeps binding to the tree it was recorded against. A Go file that cannot be parsed exits non-zero. `make fmt` remains available to developers and is never called from a verification path.
non_goals: Reformatting any Go file in this change
Replacing golangci-lint or adding new linters
Changing Makefile targets or the developer `make fmt` workflow
Pinning or asserting a specific Go or gofmt version in the script
Touching any proxy, policy, audit or workflow logic beyond the Lint job step
